title: Sharing Data with a Service
summary: Let far-apart components communicate through a shared service.
heading: Sharing Data with a Service

blocks.text: Inputs and outputs are perfect between a parent and its direct child. But when data must travel through many levels — or between two components that aren't related at all — passing it down through every layer ("prop drilling") gets painful and brittle.

blocks.caption: Threading data through every level vs. one shared service.

blocks.text: A providedIn: 'root' service is a single shared instance. Put the state in it as signals, and any component — however deep or unrelated — can read and update the same data.

blocks.label: cart.service.ts

blocks.text: A product list (deep in one part of the tree) adds items; a cart badge (in the header) shows the count. They never talk to each other — they both just use the service.

blocks.label: product.ts
cart-badge.ts

blocks.text: Because both injected the same singleton, adding in one place updates the badge instantly — no inputs, outputs, or shared parent needed.
For one-off events (a toast message, a "refresh" ping) rather than stored state, expose a Subject from the service. Components subscribe to react.

blocks.label: notify.service.ts
anywhere

items: Use inputs/outputs for direct parent ↔ child; use a service for far-apart or unrelated components.
A providedIn: 'root' service is one shared instance for everyone.
Hold shared state as signals (with computed for derived values).
Any component injects the service and reads/updates the same data.
For events instead of state, expose a Subject and subscribe.
